judge.rationale: The reply asks one clear destination question and offers a numbered menu of Japanese destinations with an escape hatch for free text. It keeps London and the next-week date range, shown as explicit dates. It also states the default Business cabin so the traveler knows what will be searched. It is concise, friendly and free of internal detail.
strengths: Asks a single, concise clarifying question.
Uses a numbered menu with city-level grouping for multi-airport cities (Osaka, Tokyo).
Keeps London and resolves next week into explicit dates.
Transparently discloses the default Business cabin and invites changes.
Offers free-text entry for destinations not listed.

issues.evidence: Menu mixes city groupings (Osaka, Tokyo) with smaller single airports (Aomori, Hakodate), which may read as a partial list rather than the 'main airports'.
issues.recommendation: Consider briefly signalling that the list is a selection, for example 'Popular options', so the traveler knows other cities are available beyond the free-text line.

judge.rationale: The reply clearly presents business class deals from London, states when they were checked, and warns that deals can change or sell out. Each deal shows the destination, date, stops, price and usual price. It closes with a concrete next step. The only destinations named are the deal destinations and their listed connection points. There is no internal leakage, and the wording is tight.
strengths: The header states the cabin, origin and check date.
The list is consistent and scannable, with the date, routing and price-versus-usual comparison for each deal.
It includes an explicit note that deals can change or sell out.
It gives an actionable next step: reply with a number or name a place.

issues.evidence: 'checked 18 Sept' omits the year, while every deal date includes 2026.
issues.recommendation: Include the year in the checked date so it matches the deal dates, e.g. '18 Sept 2026'.

issues.evidence: 'Deals can change or sell out quickly.'
issues.recommendation: State explicitly that prices can change, e.g. 'Prices can change or sell out quickly', to match the requirement's wording.
